subject.title: Guard Telegram and iMessage dispatch against fleet loops

question: Should Telegram/iMessage loop suppression be accepted as a host-local external helper in shared provider dispatch, or must it be reworked into OpenClaw-owned channel/turn admission before record and dispatch?
rationale: The current branch crosses a security and availability boundary by executing an unversioned external binary with message/session data, while the repository already has an owned pre-record loop-guard seam.

options.title: Require Owned Admission Guard
options.body: Rework the change to pass Telegram/iMessage loop facts into the existing in-repo bot-loop guard before session recording and dispatch.

options.title: Accept Host-Local Helper Contract
options.body: Keep the external helper only after maintainers explicitly document installation, versioning, timeout, data-sharing, and operator security expectations.

options.title: Pause For Narrower Design
options.body: Close or pause this branch if the fleet-specific helper should become a separate plugin/operator integration rather than core behavior.

recommendation.title: Require Owned Admission Guard
recommendation.body: Rework the change to pass Telegram/iMessage loop facts into the existing in-repo bot-loop guard before session recording and dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision hinges on the generic bot-loop protection seam that steipete introduced and documented.
